_about: Brie's moments, observations, Look around words and away lines.
Moments use the same format as content/dialogue (pages, choices, ignore); Brie's name shows on the box. Every moment needs 2 to 5 choices,
Choices are shown in a random order each time. tier and max_tier the same: the moment only happens at that bond level.
and it waits for your answer (the cat stays put). ignore is the quiet choice used only if you leave the café while it's open; it is never shown as an extra choice.
When a moment can happen (all optional): tier (lowest: stranger, curious, familiar, friend, your_cat), max_tier (highest),
when (parts of the day: late night, dawn, morning, afternoon, evening, night), weather (clear, cloudy, drizzle, rain, heavy_rain, fog, snow),
poses (her pose when it starts; left out: awake), spots (where she is),
drink ("any" or a drink id, like cafe_creme), comes_to (she moves to this spot first, if her bond allows it).
What it does: each choice has a bond (how much closer it brings her; can be negative) and a manner (calm or sudden).
then: what she does afterwards (stay, sit, loaf, sleep, leave, away), for the whole moment or for one choice.
Observations are small lines with no choices, shown in Look around when you look at her; text can be a list to pick from. Same conditions as moments.
Keep each page short: about 3 lines of 46 letters at most. An observation plus her look line should fit 4 lines.
look: what you see and can do when you look at her (Esc menu, Look around).
looks: how she looks, by tier (the highest one she has reached is shown). doing: what she's up to, by pose; {where} is her spot in words (content/look.json).
actions: things you can do, each from a tier (curious and up; strangers get none). Same fields as choices (bond, manner, then)
plus reply (what happens, a page or two), poses (her pose; left out: awake), drink, comes_to.
Each cat offers one action each time you look around; after it, the panel ends with a quiet observation about her (one without "you" in it) instead.
rest: shown if you look around again while she is still resting (4 café minutes after an action).
away: what she was like while you were away, for the note when you come back (content/narrator/away.json).
bond: new (stranger or curious), knows (familiar or friend) or yours (your cat). gone: short (under long_from_hours) or long.

pages: Brie lets out a long, dramatic sigh.
Brie sighs. It goes on for quite a while.
She glances at you, as if you should do something about it.
Brie is looking at you. Not at you, exactly. Past you, actually.
Brie watches the rain run down the glass.
She sighs. In her opinion, Paris should be dry.
Brie's nose twitches. She has noticed your café crème.
She looks at the cup, then at you, then at the cup.
Brie grooms one of her paws with great care, then another.
When she's done, she looks very pleased with herself.
Brie closes her eyes slowly, then opens them again.
From a cat, that's a compliment.
Brie jumps onto your table and settles down beside your drink, as if it was in her place.
She doesn't look at you. But she stays, glancing at your book every now and then.
Brie settles against your arm and starts to purr, very quietly.
She would never say so, but she likes you best.
Brie walks past your table without looking at you.
Then she walks past again, slower.
Brie sits on the floor and looks at the empty chair across from you. Then at you. Then at the chair.

choices.text: Pull the chair out for her

pages: A tuft of cream fur drifts past your nose. Across the room, Brie looks innocent.
Brie looks at the book on your table, then at you, as if your taste in books were a disappointment.
Brie sits on the sill with her back to the room.
She is watching the rain, and she would like everyone to know it.

choices.text: Ask if she likes the rain

pages: Brie yawns, very slowly, without covering her mouth. She seems to find you boring.

choices.text: Read her a line from your book

pages: Brie lifts her nose. She can smell your café crème from across the room.
She thinks slightly better of you.

choices.text: Hide the cup behind your book

pages: Brie settles by the lamp on the sideboard, in the warmest spot in the room.
She closes her eyes, then opens one to check on you.

choices.text: Turn the page of your book

pages: Brie's tail swishes once, twice. Something you did has displeased her. You aren't sure what.
Brie walks across the café as if she owned it. To be fair, she might.
Brie's collar has twisted round. She is pretending she hasn't noticed.
A patch of sun falls on the sill. Brie moves into it with great dignity, one paw at a time.

choices.text: Turn your chair to the sun too

pages: Brie watches you drink. When you put the cup down, she sighs, as if you've done it wrong.
Brie kneads the cushion in the cat bed for a long time.
Then she sits next to it instead.

choices.text: Tell her it looks very comfortable

pages: Brie sneezes. Then she looks around to see if anyone saw.

choices.text: Sneeze too, to keep her company

pages: Brie has come close enough to read over your shoulder. She doesn't think much of the chapter.

choices.text: Hold the book a little lower

pages: The rain is so loud that Brie flattens her ears.
She glares at the window as if it were being rude on purpose.
Brie stretches, front paws far ahead, back legs far behind. It takes a while. Everybody waits.
Brie sits as close as she dares to your café crème and looks at the ceiling, as if the cup weren't there.

choices.text: Tell her it's very good today
Pull the cup closer to you

pages: Brie lies by the lamp with her paws tucked in.
Every few minutes she lets out a small sigh, to remind the room she's there.
Brie jumps onto the chair across from you and sits as if she had a reservation.

choices.text: Nod, as to an old acquaintance
Tell her that seat is taken

pages: Brie licks a paw and smooths down a bit of fur on her forehead. She looks at you to check it worked.

choices.text: Point out the bit she missed

pages: Brie sits on the sill and moves over, a little, as if someone might want to join her.

choices.text: Lean over and look out with her

pages: Brie flops onto her side with a heavy sigh, as if the whole day had been too much.

choices.text: Offer your scarf as a pillow

pages: Your bookmark has fallen on the floor. Brie is sitting next to it, looking innocent.

choices.text: Pick it up and thank her

pages: Brie watches the snow fall past the window.
Her tail curls round her paws, and she looks almost happy.

choices.text: Tell her it matches her fur
Ask if she's ever been out in it
Draw a cat on the misty glass

pages: Brie starts to purr, then seems to remember herself and stops.

choices.text: Tell her it's all right to purr

pages: Brie sits by the lamp on the sideboard. In its light her fur looks almost gold. She knows.

choices.text: Ask her to hold that pose

pages: Brie has found a sugar cube on the floor.
She pushes it towards you with her nose, as if you'd dropped it.
The Eiffel Tower lights up. Brie turns to look at it, then back at you, as if to say: you're welcome.
Brie lies down across your open book.
You can't read any more, and that seems to be the idea.

choices.text: Close the book and give up
Read the bit you can see

pages: Brie sits beside your cup and watches every sip go by, very seriously.
Brie walks past your chair and bumps her head against your hand.
Then she keeps walking, as if it were an accident.

choices.text: Scratch her ears as she goes
Pretend it was an accident too

pages: Brie lets out the longest sigh yet. Then she looks at you, as if it's your turn.

choices.text: Complain about the weather with her
Ask if it's really that bad

pages: Brie looks at you and closes her eyes, very slowly. She keeps them closed a long time.
Brie puts one front paw on your knee and looks up at you. She is considering it.
Brie sits beside your chair and purrs, quietly, while the windows across the street light up one by one.
Brie sits by your café crème and reaches a paw towards the foam.
She stops just short of it and looks at you.

choices.text: Wipe her paw with a napkin

pages: Brie licks your hand twice, then stops. You have been groomed. It wasn't optional.

choices.text: Groom her back with your fingers

pages: Brie is asleep with her tail over her nose. Now and then, she sighs in her sleep.
Brie walks across the café and settles against your ankle, as if that's simply where she goes now.
Brie lies down beside your book, puts her chin on the page and falls asleep.
Brie sighs her long, theatrical sigh.
But this time she's looking at you, and she's purring.

choices.text: Tell her you missed her too

pages: Brie sits by your café crème as if she were guarding it from the rest of the café.

choices.text: Ask who she's guarding it from

pages: Brie rubs her cheek along your book, then your hand, then the book again.
Everything here is hers now.

choices.text: Ask if that includes the book

pages: Brie calls to you from the windowsill: one short, polite meow. She wants you to see something.
It's raining again. Brie doesn't sigh this time. She just curls up closer to you.

choices.text: Tell her it's cosy like this

pages: It's very late. Brie sits by your feet and looks at the door, then at you, as if to say: not yet.

choices.text: Tell her you're not going yet
Pick her up for a cuddle

pages: Brie grooms herself on your table, very thoroughly, and now and then grooms your sleeve by mistake.

choices.text: Tell her she missed a spot

pages: Brie greets you with a soft chirp you've never heard her make. She looks a little embarrassed.

choices.text: Ask her to do it again

observations.text: Brie is sitting very straight, like a little statue.
Brie is grooming her chest fluff.

text: Brie is asleep, her tail over her face.

observations.text: Brie watches a raindrop, and sighs.
Brie has found the warm spot by the lamp.

looks.stranger: A fluffy cream cat with odd eyes, one blue, one amber. She pretends not to have noticed you.
looks.curious: Brie, fluffy and cream, with odd eyes. She keeps an eye on you. The blue one.
looks.familiar: Brie. Her fur is softer than it looks, and her collar is a little crooked.
looks.friend: Brie, your elegant friend. She lets you look as long as you like.
looks.your_cat: Brie, who has decided that you are hers.

doing.stand: She stands {where}, deciding where to go next.
doing.loaf: She is lying {where}, paws tucked in.
doing.sleep: She is asleep {where}, her tail over her face.

look.rest: Brie has had enough attention for now.

reply: Brie sniffs your fingers, then looks away, as if they weren't worth the trouble.
Brie flicks an ear. That counts as a hello.
You leave Brie to her nap. Her tail twitches once.
Brie arches into your hand, just once.
Then she sits down again, very dignified.

actions.text: Let her smell your café crème
reply: Brie sniffs the cup for a long moment, then sighs. Approved.
Brie closes her eyes and lifts her chin a little higher.
Brie takes her time. Then she jumps onto your table and settles down beside your drink.

actions.text: Run your fingers through her fur
reply: Brie purrs, very quietly, so nobody else hears.

away.text: Brie hasn't moved from her spot. She doesn't seem to have noticed you left.
Brie is grooming. She looks up, then goes back to it.
Brie gives you a long look, as if trying to remember where she's seen you.
Brie is on the windowsill, where she always is. She doesn't look round.
Brie looks at you as if you were late.
Brie sighs when you sit down. You were gone a bit long, apparently.
Brie turns her back to you when you come in. Then she looks over her shoulder, to make sure you saw.
Brie pretends she didn't miss you. She isn't very good at it.
Brie kept your chair warm. She isn't happy about giving it back.
Brie flicks her tail when she sees you. From her, that's a warm welcome.
Brie meets you at the door, sighs very loudly, and walks you to your table.
Brie has been sitting in your chair. She gets down, slowly, when you arrive.
